title: Deposition of Marcus T. Holloway
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS
224TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-56789

MARCUS T. HOLLOWAY, PLAINTIFF
v.
PETRO-TEX REFINING CO., DEFENDANT

---

DEPOSITION EXCERPT

Taken on behalf of the Plaintiff, Marcus T. Holloway, on the 12th day of March, 2025, at 10:00 a.m., at the offices of Smith & Associates, 100 Main Street, Houston, Texas 77002.

Present:
Marcus T. Holloway, Plaintiff
Lydia O’Neil, Attorney for Plaintiff
Rebecca Chen-Whitfield, Attorney for Defendant
Judge Arthur T. Graves (presiding via telephone conference)

---

Lydia O’Neil: Mr. Holloway, please state your full name and date of birth for the record.

Marcus Holloway: Marcus Theodore Holloway. My date of birth is August 5, 1978.

Lydia O’Neil: And your current address?

Marcus Holloway: 1423 Oakwood Lane, Apt. 4B, Houston, Texas 77004.

Lydia O’Neil: Thank you. Now, Mr. Holloway, you were employed by Petro-Tex Refining Co. from March 2019 until your termination in November 2024, correct?

Marcus Holloway: Yes, that's right.

Lydia O’Neil: What was your position?

Marcus Holloway: I was a shift supervisor in the cracking unit.

Lydia O’Neil: And can you describe the incident that led to your termination?

Marcus Holloway: On November 5, 2024, I reported a safety violation involving improper storage of volatile chemicals. My supervisor, a man named David Holloway—no relation, by the way—told me to keep quiet. I refused, and I was fired the next day.

Rebecca Chen-Whitfield: Objection, form. Move to strike the witness's characterization.

Judge Arthur T. Graves: Sustained. The jury will disregard the statement about being fired as a result of the report. Mr. Holloway, please just describe the events.

Marcus Holloway: Sorry, Your Honor. I reported the violation to David Holloway. He said, quote, 'Mind your own business, Marcus.' I then sent an email to the safety committee. That's when things got ugly.

Lydia O’Neil: What happened after you sent that email?

Marcus Holloway: I was called into a meeting with HR and given a termination notice. They said I had violated company policy by insubordination. But I think it was retaliation.

Rebecca Chen-Whitfield: Your Honor, I object. This witness is speculating.

Judge Arthur T. Graves: Sustained. The witness will stick to facts.

Lydia O’Neil: Mr. Holloway, do you have any evidence of retaliation?

Marcus Holloway: Yes. I have copies of emails, including one from David Holloway where he wrote, 'If you don't drop this, you'll be sorry.' I kept everything.

Lydia O’Neil: And what about your personnel file? Did you request it?

Marcus Holloway: I did. But they refused to give it to me, citing confidentiality. I had to hire a lawyer to get it.

Rebecca Chen-Whitfield: Objection, hearsay.

Judge Arthur T. Graves: Overruled. Continue.

Lydia O’Neil: Mr. Holloway, have you ever been disciplined before this incident?

Marcus Holloway: No. I had a clean record. In fact, I received a commendation in 2022 for safety improvements.

Rebecca Chen-Whitfield: Your Honor, I move to strike the answer as non-responsive.

Judge Arthur T. Graves: Sustained. The witness will answer only the question asked.

Lydia O’Neil: Let me rephrase. Mr. Holloway, did you receive any written warnings prior to November 2024?

Marcus Holloway: No, I did not.

Lydia O’Neil: And your Social Security number? For the record, please state the last four digits.

Marcus Holloway: It’s 123-45-6789. But I’d rather not say the whole thing.

Lydia O’Neil: That's fine. The last four digits are sufficient. Now, Mr. Holloway, you mentioned a David Holloway. Can you spell his last name?

Marcus Holloway: H-O-L-L-O-W-A-Y. Same as mine, but we’re not related.

Lydia O’Neil: Thank you. Now, did you ever file a complaint with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration?

Marcus Holloway: Yes, I did. I filed online. The case number is OSHA-2024-09876.

Rebecca Chen-Whitfield: Objection. Relevance?

Judge Arthur T. Graves: Overruled. The witness may answer.

Lydia O’Neil: And what was the outcome?

Marcus Holloway: They investigated and found multiple violations. They fined Petro-Tex $50,000. That's in the report.

Lydia O’Neil: I have no further questions at this time.

Rebecca Chen-Whitfield: Your Honor, I’d like to reserve my cross-examination for a later date.

Judge Arthur T. Graves: So ordered. This deposition is adjourned.

---

[1] The witness's personnel file was marked as Defendant's Exhibit A for identification.
[2] The OSHA report is attached as Plaintiff's Exhibit B.

---

FOOTNOTE BLOCK:

[1] Defendant's Exhibit A: Personnel file of Marcus T. Holloway, dated November 10, 2024.
[2] Plaintiff's Exhibit B: OSHA Inspection Report No. 2024-09876, dated December 15, 2024.

---

CERTIFICATION

I, Lydia O’Neil, certify that the foregoing is a true and correct excerpt of the deposition of Marcus T. Holloway, taken on March 12, 2025.

/s/ Lydia O’Neil

---

Reporter Citations:
Smith v. Jones, 123 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Houston 2005)
Doe v. Petro-Tex, 456 F.3d 789 (5th Cir. 2006)

Statute Section:
Tex. Lab. Code § 21.055 (retaliation)
